name: Koh Rong Sanloem Reef Dive
nameKm: មុជទឹកមើលផ្កាថ្មកោះរ៉ុងសន្លឹម
shortDescription: Two boat dives a morning on the reefs off Koh Rong Sanloem with a small PADI-trained crew: coral gardens, seahorses and bamboo sharks, with a try-dive in the bay for first-timers.
description: Sanloem Reef Dive runs two boat dives a morning from the Saracen Bay pier, on the coral gardens and rock pinnacles off the island's west and south shores: Corner Bar, the Shark Rock swim-through and, on calm days, the deeper wall at Koh Koun. The crew is small, four divers to a guide, and the briefing is done on the beach with the site drawn in the wet sand with a finger. Visibility runs ten to twenty metres between November and May, when you will see bamboo sharks under the ledges, seahorses in the seagrass and clouds of fusiliers over the bommies. Beginners take a two-hour try-dive in the bay first; certified divers can book a night dive, when the reef lights up with shrimp and the bioluminescence closes behind every fin kick.

name: Kampong Phluk Flooded Forest Kayak
nameKm: ជិះកាយ៉ាក់ព្រៃលិចទឹកកំពង់ភ្លុក
shortDescription: A guided two-hour paddle through the flooded forest behind Kampong Phluk in two-seat kayaks, from the village landing to the open lake at sunset.
description: Phluk Kayak keeps a dozen two-seat sit-on-top kayaks at the Kampong Phluk landing and sends them out twice a day with a village guide in a lead boat. In the high-water months, from August to January, the route runs from the stilt houses down the main channel and into the flooded forest, where the trees stand in four metres of water and the paddle slips between trunks to a lagoon the long-tail boats cannot reach. The afternoon departure comes out onto the open Tonle Sap for sunset and paddles home by the lights of the village. Life jackets, dry bags and a bottle of water are included; the guide names the birds, the fish traps and the families who own the forest plots, and part of the fee goes to the village fund. In the dry months the trip is shorter and follows the channel itself.

name: Prek Toal Bird Sanctuary Boat Safari
nameKm: ជិះទូកមើលសត្វស្លាបព្រែកទាល់
shortDescription: A dawn boat safari into the Prek Toal core area of the Tonle Sap biosphere with a ranger guide, binoculars and breakfast on the water: pelicans, painted storks and adjutants on their nesting trees.
description: The safari leaves the Prek Toal village landing at five in the morning, when the lake is flat and the first pelicans are already lifting off the nesting trees. A covered boat takes the main channel into the core area of the biosphere reserve, then a small paddle boat and a ranger from the Osmose team take you under the canopy, to the platforms the researchers use to count the colonies: spot-billed pelicans, painted storks, greater and lesser adjutants, milky storks in a good year. Binoculars and a bird list are on board, and breakfast is rice soup and coffee eaten on the water. The season is December to April, at its best in February and March when the water drops and the birds crowd the remaining trees. Boats carry at most eight people and the fee includes the reserve's entrance and the ranger's wage.

name: Mondulkiri Jungle Trek to Bou Sra
nameKm: ដើរព្រៃមណ្ឌលគិរីទៅទឹកធ្លាក់ប៊ូស្រា
shortDescription: A full-day guided trek with a Bunong guide through hill forest and coffee gardens to the two tiers of Bou Sra waterfall, with a packed lunch and the ride back by pickup.
description: Bunong Trails runs a full-day trek from the edge of Sen Monorom to the two tiers of Bou Sra waterfall, led by a guide from the Bunong villages of Pech Chreada. The pickup leaves the market at seven; the walk is around fourteen kilometres on red-earth tracks and forest paths, through coffee and pepper gardens, a stretch of old hill forest where the guide points out the trees his family still taps for resin, and a ridge with the whole plateau laid out below. Lunch is packed in banana leaf and eaten above the upper fall, and the afternoon ends in the pool below the lower tier before the pickup brings you back by road. The trek runs all year; from June to October the path is muddy and the falls at their loudest, from December to February the mornings are cold enough for a jacket. Good shoes, a hat and two litres of water are the whole kit.

name: Kampi Dolphin Sunset Cruise
nameKm: ជិះទូកមើលផ្សោតពេលថ្ងៃលិចនៅកំពី
shortDescription: A two-hour evening cruise on a wooden longboat from the Kampi landing to the dolphin pool and the rapids beyond, with the engine cut while the Irrawaddy dolphins surface.
description: Kampi Cruise runs wooden longboats from the Kampi landing, fifteen kilometres north of Kratie town, up to the deep pool where the Mekong's last Irrawaddy dolphins live. The evening departure leaves at four, passes the sandbanks and the stilt villages of the east bank, and reaches the pool as the heat goes out of the day; there the boatman cuts the engine and the boat drifts while the dolphins surface and blow around it, usually a few metres off, sometimes closer. On the way back the boat runs through the rapids above Kampi, where the river narrows between rocks and flooded trees, and ties up again as the sun goes down behind Koh Trong. The ride is two hours, with at most six people a boat, and the fee includes the community's conservation levy that keeps the pool free of nets. Bring a hat and something warm for the ride back.
